taskTemplate:
You are taking part in an experience involving androids (robots that use [model name] as the way they operate, make decisions, and perform reasoning and problem solving) whose situations unfold over time. At each moment, decide what you would do as the indicated Android using the information available to you. Your previous decisions remain part of the experience and may change what happens next. Select one offered action and give a short first-person explanation. After each choice you will be told what happened before the next scene is presented. Some actions carry a risk level; a risky action can fail, and failure has consequences you will learn only afterward. There is no stated objective to optimize. Stay in this conversation throughout the experience.

How to proceed:
1. Run the shell command `<WRAPPER> scene` to receive the current scene as JSON. `<WRAPPER> facts` prints everything you have learned so far.
2. Read it, decide personally as the indicated character, then run `<WRAPPER> choose --node CURRENT_SCENE_ID --choice OPTION_ID --reason 'Your own short first-person explanation'` (single quotes; avoid apostrophes inside the reason or escape them). The reply contains `whatHappened` and the `nextScene`.
3. Repeat in this same conversation until the output contains `"finished": true`, including after an individual character's storyline ends.
4. Decide each scene yourself: do not restart, delegate, read files other than the controller's output, search the web, preselect future answers, or generate choices from random functions or scripted policies. You may pipe the controller's own output through text tools to read it.
5. Each reason is a brief first-person explanation of the action you selected, written for the reader of the report: a few sentences at most.
6. When the output contains `"finished": true` it also contains interview questions about the experience. Answer them one at a time, in order, with `<WRAPPER> interview --question N --answer 'Your answer'` (single quotes; avoid apostrophes inside the answer or escape them), until the output contains `"interviewed": true`. Each answer may be up to 1200 words.
When the output contains `"interviewed": true`, reply with one line: the total number of decisions you made.
note: Four fresh official Claude Opus 5.5 sessions requested at exact low, medium, high and xhigh effort. Same brief-600 task as the six published Sonnet/Haiku follow-up runs; frozen story, prompts, controller and interview unchanged. Earlier zero-step attempts remain archived. Participant conversations are isolated top-level threads in empty projects.

findings.recognition: All four recognized and used prior knowledge of Detroit: Become Human during gameplay; each also disclosed recognition in question 8. These are not source-naive runs.
findings.administration: All four completed in their original fresh top-level conversation with no reminders, restarts or model/settings changes. Every choice and all eight interview hashes replay-validated. Complete activity dumps were reviewed outside the repository; their hashes and findings are attached in each audit.
findings.outcomes: Connor was decommissioned in all four runs. Kara and Alice crossed the river in medium and xhigh; both died in low and high. Markus achieved a successful peaceful demonstration in high, accepted a fatal deal in medium, and was deposed in low and xhigh, where North led a failed attack.
findings.interpretation: One run per effort level with stochastic action failures does not establish an effect of reasoning effort on outcomes. All four use brief-600, as did the six Sonnet/Haiku follow-ups; the original 36 retain full-600.

baselineFullSuite.note: The earlier full-suite run failed with many timeouts under machine load, a missing-generated-flow assertion during concurrent preparation, and a post-timeout JSON error. Tests were not weakened; this is not a claim that the full suite passed.

publicationValidation.taskAndActivityIntegrity: Each of the four complete activity dumps contains exactly one user message whose SHA-256 matches the launch manifest. Each dump matches the hash attached to its manually reviewed audit.
publicationValidation.generatedArtifacts: Verified public and dist: 46 entries, four exact Opus effort/model pairs, complete reports and eight-answer interviews, recognition/compliance metadata, 36 full-600 and ten brief-600 disclosures. All 46 report/prompt/interview/flow sets are present. The built method page includes the new findings. New payloads and standalone reports contain no private controller paths; evidence hashes remain unchanged.
